newsitem.title: USA: Hawaiian Tropic founder sued for sexual harassment.
newsitem.headline: Hawaiian Tropic founder sued for sexual harassment.

text.p: Ron Rice, creator of Hawaiian Tropic skin care products, which are promoted by buxom, bikini-clad Hawaiian Tropic Girls, has been sued by his former secretary for sexual harassment, her lawyer said on Thursday.

Kelley King, 35, accused Rice in a lawsuit filed on Monday in circuit court of harassing her throughout her 12-year career. She also alleged age discrimination, claiming Rice restricted her opportunities for raises and promotions as she grew older.
Similar complaints by King are on file with the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and the Florida Commission on Human Relations, her attorney, Jimmy Charles, said.

In her lawsuit, she accused Rice of making repeated and unwanted sexual advances, including inappropriate touching and lewd comments. The suit alleged that Rice often demeaned his female employees and called them things like "dingo brains" or "honey bees."
"All of these women are very intimidated," Charles said. "They were awed by the wealth and glamour of Ron Rice and Hawaiian Tropic."
King also alleged she was required to perform a number of menial tasks such as delivering one of Rice's stool samples to his doctor.
Rice was travelling Thursday and unavailable for comment. A company executive, Bill Jennings, said Rice did not plan to comment until he had been served with documents and had time to examine them.

Rice is sole owner of Hawaiian Tropic, with sales of about $200 million a year. His net worth is estimated at $100 million. He was a lifeguard in 1965 when he started to sell his homemade suntan lotion from the back of his Mustang convertible.
He does not advertise his products through traditional means, relying on the "Hawaiian Tropic Girls" and his sponsorship of events ranging from bikini contests to auto racing.
